text: The view running from Locke through Parfit, on which a later person is the same person as an earlier one in virtue of overlapping chains of memories, beliefs, and intentions, is called the ___ theory of personal identity.
explanation: Psychological continuity theory grounds identity in overlapping chains of psychological connectedness (Parfit's refinement of Locke's memory criterion). It is standardly contrasted with the biological/animalist criterion (same organism) and with the further-fact/soul view.
